questions.prompt: Which branch of natural science studies the properties and changes of substances?
questions.explanation: Chemistry is the study of the properties, composition, and changes of substances.

questions.prompt: A testable guess that a scientist makes before doing an experiment is called a:
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a testable guess or possible explanation that a scientist checks by experiment.

questions.prompt: Combining biology and chemistry to study the chemical reactions that happen inside living things forms which field?
questions.explanation: Biochemistry combines biology and chemistry to study the chemical reactions that take place inside living organisms.

questions.prompt: A laboratory report records an experiment. Which order of steps is correct?
questions.explanation: A proper lab report moves from the objective, to the procedure, to the observation, and finally to the conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter takes the shape of its container but keeps a fixed volume?
questions.explanation: A liquid takes the shape of its container because its particles can slide past each other, but it keeps a fixed volume.

questions.prompt: When solid ice is heated and turns into liquid water, this change is called:
questions.explanation: Melting is the change from a solid to a liquid when heat is added, such as ice turning into water.

questions.prompt: A spoon of sugar is stirred into a cup of tea until it can no longer be seen. The result is best described as a:
questions.explanation: The dissolved sugar spreads evenly and looks the same throughout the tea, so it forms a homogeneous mixture (a solution).

questions.prompt: Why is milk turning sour considered a chemical change?
options: The milk only changes its container shape
A new substance with new properties is formed
The milk can easily be turned back fresh
questions.explanation: Souring forms new substances with a new taste and smell and cannot be reversed, so it is a chemical change.

questions.prompt: To collect pure drinking water from salty water, you boil it and then cool the steam back into liquid. This method is:
questions.explanation: Distillation boils a liquid to vapour and then cools the vapour back to a pure liquid, leaving the dissolved salt behind.

questions.prompt: What is the correct chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: The symbol for sodium is Na, taken from its Latin name 'natrium'.

questions.prompt: In a chemical equation, the new substances formed on the right of the arrow are called the:
questions.explanation: The products are the new substances formed in a reaction and are written on the right side of the arrow.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a metal element?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal, which is shiny and conducts electricity. Oxygen, carbon, and sulfur are non-metals.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are present in one unit of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃?
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ has 1 calcium, 1 carbon, and 3 oxygen atoms, giving a total of 5 atoms.

questions.prompt: Which is the correctly balanced equation for nitrogen reacting with hydrogen to form ammonia (NH₃)?
questions.explanation: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ has 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms on each side, so it is balanced.

questions.prompt: The symbols 'Co' and 'CO' mean different things. Which statement is correct?
options: Co is the element cobalt, while CO is the compound carbon monoxide
CO is an element and Co is a mixture
questions.explanation: Capital letters matter: Co (capital then small) is the element cobalt, while CO (two capitals) is carbon monoxide, a compound of carbon and oxygen.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Which part of a microscope is the flat platform where the slide is placed?
questions.explanation: The stage is the flat platform on which the slide holding the specimen is placed.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Which structure in a plant cell traps sunlight to make food?
questions.explanation: The chloroplast contains chlorophyll, which traps sunlight so the plant can make food by photosynthesis.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Which knob on a microscope is used last to make the image sharp and clear?
questions.explanation: The fine adjustment knob moves the tube only a tiny amount and is used to make the image perfectly sharp after the coarse knob.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: A microscope gives a total magnification of 100 times. If the eyepiece magnifies 10 times, what is the magnification of the objective lens used?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective, so 100 ÷ 10 = 10, meaning the objective magnifies 10 times.

questions.topic: Cell as the Basis of Life
questions.prompt: Why does a plant cell keep a firm, fixed shape while an animal cell does not?
options: A plant cell has no cytoplasm
A plant cell has a strong, rigid cell wall
An animal cell has more mitochondria
An animal cell has a larger nucleus
questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall around a plant cell gives it shape and support; animal cells have only a flexible membrane, so they have no fixed shape.

questions.prompt: The ability of a living thing to respond to changes around it, such as a plant growing towards light, is called:
questions.explanation: Sensitivity is the ability to respond to changes in the surroundings, one of the MRS GREN characteristics of living things.

questions.prompt: Yeast, which is used to make bread rise, belongs to which kingdom?
questions.explanation: Yeast is a fungus; like other fungi it cannot make its own food and belongs to Kingdom Fungi.

questions.prompt: Which kingdom contains mostly single-celled organisms that DO have a true nucleus, such as the amoeba?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Protista contains mostly single-celled organisms that have a true nucleus, such as amoeba and algae.

questions.prompt: In classifying living things, which list goes correctly from the LARGEST group to a smaller group?
questions.explanation: The order from largest to smallest is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species, so Kingdom → Phylum → Class is correct.

questions.prompt: A river flows, carries soil, and can grow wider over time, yet scientists say it is NOT alive. Why?
options: It does not move at all
It does not show all the characteristics of living things, such as reproduction and nutrition
questions.explanation: A thing is alive only if it shows all the MRS GREN characteristics. A river cannot reproduce, take in food, or excrete, so it is not living.

questions.prompt: All the living things on Earth together make up which part of the Earth system?
questions.explanation: The biosphere includes all the living things on Earth, on land, in water, and in the air.

questions.prompt: About how long does the Earth take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
questions.explanation: One revolution of the Earth around the Sun takes about 365¼ days, which is one year.

questions.prompt: In the water cycle, the Sun heats water in lakes and oceans so it turns into water vapour. This stage is called:
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when the Sun's heat turns liquid water into water vapour that rises into the air.

questions.prompt: When a ship sails away from shore, the bottom of the ship disappears from view before the top. What does this observation suggest?
questions.explanation: Because the Earth's surface is curved, the lower part of a distant ship is hidden first, which is evidence that the Earth is round.

questions.prompt: The solid inner core of the Earth is made mostly of iron and nickel and is extremely hot, yet it stays solid. The best reason is that:
options: It is far from the Sun
The enormous pressure deep inside keeps it solid
It is made of cool rock
It contains a lot of water
questions.explanation: Even though the inner core is very hot, the huge pressure at the centre of the Earth keeps it in a solid state.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: The energy stored in food, fuel, and batteries is called:
questions.explanation: Chemical energy is the energy stored in substances such as food, fuel, and batteries.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: A child swinging back and forth on a swing is an example of which type of motion?
questions.explanation: Oscillatory (vibrational) motion is repeated back-and-forth movement, like a swing or a pendulum.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: Gravity pulling a falling mango towards the ground is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Gravity acts from a distance without the objects touching, so it is a non-contact force.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: When a person plays a drum, electrical signals are not involved. The main energy change is from:
questions.explanation: The moving hand hitting the drum (kinetic energy) makes the drum skin vibrate, which produces sound energy.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: Which list contains ONLY non-renewable energy sources?
questions.explanation: Coal, oil, and natural gas are all non-renewable because they take millions of years to form and will eventually run out.

questions.topic: Motion, Force, Energy and Energy Resources
questions.prompt: An object is taken from Earth to the Moon, where gravity is weaker. What happens to its mass and weight?
options: Mass stays the same, but weight becomes smaller
Mass becomes smaller, but weight stays the same
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter and never changes, but weight is the force of gravity, so it becomes smaller where gravity is weaker.
